fact_label: Limitations item L3 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values:
- TabNet may be hurt by our schedule. Corrected as of 2026-11-07 from diagnostics JSONs (`results/diagnostics/*__{model}__*.json`, key `"0.1"`): at fraction 0.1, `patience_epochs` is **12 to 20** (not 5 to 8) and the validation part (`n_val`) is **4 to 9 rows** (not 5 to 8) — this applies to all three deep models (mlp/ftt/tabnet), since they share the same `training_schedule` function, not just TabNet. The 600-step cap is correct (`MAX_STEPS=600` in `src/deep_models.py`). About a third of MLP runs at fraction 1.0 hit the step/epoch cap — confirmed: 17/50 (34%) of `mlp` fraction-1.0 tasks have `epochs_run >= max_epochs` in their diagnostics file.
  **Phase 2c sensitivity-check outcome** (`scripts/phase2c_diagnostics.py sensitivity`, 360 fits, splits 0-2 only): TabNet's known collapse on `ckd` at fraction 1.0 (baseline mean AUROC 0.919, split std 0.138) **disappears** under all three longer-schedule/bigger-validation variants tested (`A_long` 2000/150/0.15, `B_bigval` 600/60/0.30, `C_long_bigval` 2000/150/0.30 for max_steps/patience_steps/validation_fraction): mean AUROC 0.999-1.000, std ≤ 0.0015. Dataset-averaged, TabNet gains +0.022 AUROC at fraction 0.1 and +0.016 at fraction 1.0 under `A_long`; MLP and FT-Transformer barely move (every change < 0.01 AUROC) — the schedule mainly affects TabNet. 0/360 fits failed, 0 NaN losses, 0 constant predictions. TabNet's `heart_cleveland` collapses (splits 1 and 7) were only partly covered by this check (split 1 is in scope, split 7 is not, since the brief scoped splits to 0-2) and did not resolve as cleanly there. Full tables: `results/phase2c/sensitivity_report_S1.csv` .. `S5.csv`.

fact_label: Limitations item L4 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values: - The classical search-space endpoint table was requested but never reported. Computed as of 2026-11-07 from `results/tuning/*.json` via `scripts/phase2c_diagnostics.py endpoints`: `xgb`'s `min_child_weight` (tuned range 1-10) hits an endpoint in 52% of its 50 tasks (23 at the lower bound of 1, 3 at the upper bound of 10); `rf`'s `min_samples_leaf` (tuned range 1-10) hits an endpoint in 42% of its 50 tasks (18 lower, 3 upper). Both are dominated by the *lower* endpoint, not evenly split. For xgb this is a **mild constraint, not a hard floor**: `min_child_weight` is a hessian-sum threshold, and for logistic loss each row contributes at most `p(1-p) ≤ 0.25` to a leaf's hessian, so `min_child_weight=1` already only requires about 4 or more rows per leaf — the lower bound of 1 is not pinning the tree to trivially small leaves. Full per-model/per-parameter table (34 parameters, 7 models): `results/phase2c/endpoints_overall.csv` and `endpoints_by_dataset.csv`. Parameters at the *same* endpoint in ≥ 15 of 50 tasks: `mlp n_layers` (39: 27 lower/12 upper), `tabnet n_d` (32: 18/14), `ftt n_blocks` (30: 15/15), `ftt d_token` (29: 9/20), `tabnet n_steps` (28: 22/6), `ftt batch_size` (28: 17/11), `xgb min_child_weight` (26: 23/3), `tabnet batch_size` (24: 12/12), `rf min_samples_leaf` (21: 18/3), `mlp batch_size` (20: 13/7), `xgb max_depth` (15: 8/7).

fact_label: Limitations item L7 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values: - **Calibration caveats (Phase 3b, 2026-11-07; full statement in `results/phase3b/calibration_notes.md`):** every pooled calibration analysis uses 2 x n_rows predictions per (dataset, model, fraction), since each test row appears in 2 of the 10 splits (one per CV repeat). ECE on small samples is biased and noisy, and equal-width (`ece_ew`) and equal-mass (`ece_em`) ECE use different binning rules (they never differed by more than 0.03 in this run, 0/140 cells). The Platt calibration slope/intercept are undefined when the two classes are exactly separable in logit space; at the pooled point-estimate level this never happened in this run (0/140 cells, even for `ckd`), but several `ckd` bootstrap replicates were separable and dropped (up to 101/2000 for `ckd`/logreg at fraction 1.0). 29/280 non-separable (dataset, model, fraction) cells have a pooled slope below 0.5 or above 2 (mostly `ckd` at fraction 1.0, where `logreg`'s slope is 10.78 and `rf`'s is 3.42, and most models at fraction 0.1). The cross-fitted post-hoc Platt/isotonic check (`scripts/phase3b_calibration.py posthoc`) is descriptive only and not part of the pipeline: isotonic regression's AUROC changed by up to 0.059-0.110 (max over individual splits) relative to the original predictions, and `logreg`'s isotonic log loss rose by about +0.21 to +0.26 dataset-averaged (isotonic can map a prediction to exactly 0 or 1 on a held-out fold, which is then clipped and penalised heavily by log loss if wrong) — Platt's fallback-to-identity rate was 439/3500 fold-fits (12.5%, single-class or separable fit folds); isotonic never fell back (0/3500).

fact_label: Limitations item L8 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values: - **Robustness caveats (Phase 3c, 2026-11-08; full statement in `results/phase3c/robustness_notes.md`):** every result describes MODEL + the saved pipeline's IMPUTER together (median/most-frequent imputation fitted on the training fold is part of the pipeline), not the model in isolation; tree models use no native NaN handling. Missingness tested is MCAR only — no informative-missingness mechanism (e.g. values missing because they are abnormal) was simulated. Noise is relative to each column's TRAINING standard deviation and applied to ordinal numeric columns (CKD `sg`/`al`/`su`, Cleveland `ca`) as if continuous. 5 independent perturbation draws per (dataset, split, kind, level); every model is evaluated on the identical perturbed matrix for a given draw. The dataset-averaged bootstrap resamples the 10 splits within each dataset and ignores between-dataset variability. Degradation is always relative to each model's OWN clean performance on that split, so a model with lower clean performance can show smaller absolute degradation.

fact_label: Limitations item L9 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values: - **Explanation and noise-variant caveats (Phase 3d, 2026-11-08; full statements in `results/phase3d/noise_continuous/robustness_notes.md` and `results/phase3d/explanation_notes.md`):** `logreg` is explained in LOG-ODDS (`decision_function`) while `rf`/`mlp` are explained in PROBABILITY of the positive class, so only RANKINGS (top-5 sets, Spearman correlation) are ever compared across models, never raw SHAP magnitudes. The `mlp` KernelExplainer uses a 50-row TRAINING background (seed 42 + split_idx) and `nsamples="auto"`. The 10 splits of a dataset come from repeated cross-validation with overlapping training sets and are therefore not independent (same caveat as Phase 3a's BLOCK unit). No direction-of-effect (positive/negative SHAP) check was performed. Correlated features — especially Breast Wisconsin's mean/standard-error/worst triplets — can substitute for one another in a top-5 set (confirmed: `breast_wisconsin`/logreg had 8 distinct top-5 sets and `breast_wisconsin`/mlp had 9, out of 10 splits). For the continuous-only noise variant: CKD's `bp` column was kept IN (noised) despite meeting the same <=10-distinct-values rule as the excluded `sg`/`al`/`su`, per Demian's explicit confirmation, not an automatic decision.

fact_label: Limitations item L10 (CLAUDE.md section 7, verbatim)
values:
- **Decisions recorded 2026-11-07 (after Phase 2c/3a):**
  1. The deep models are **not** rerun with a longer schedule; the primary results use the baseline training schedule (`MAX_STEPS=600`, `PATIENCE_STEPS=60`, `VALIDATION_FRACTION=0.15`). The Phase 2c 360-fit schedule-sensitivity check is reported only as a supplementary analysis, with the caveats that it used 3 splits (0-2, not all 10), fractions 0.1 and 1.0 only (not 0.25/0.5), no re-tuning of hyperparameters under the new schedule, and that the schedule variants were not chosen by looking at test AUROC.
  2. The classical `xgb` `min_child_weight` wide-range check (0.1 to 10 log-uniform, 3 datasets x 3 splits; results in `results/phase2c/xgb_wide_range.csv`, **not** `results/phase3c`) showed **no consistent change** in test AUROC — the sign of (wide AUROC − original AUROC) is mixed across datasets, splits and fractions. No classical rerun is planned.
  3. Endpoint findings by the same-endpoint rule (full table: `results/phase2c/endpoints_overall.csv`): `xgb min_child_weight` 23/50 at the lower bound; `mlp n_layers` 27/50 lower; `tabnet n_steps` 22/50 lower; `ftt d_token` 20/50 at the upper bound (64, the top of its `[16, 32, 64]` choices — a limitation of possible truncation applies only to `ftt d_token`, since it is the only one of these five where the upper endpoint, not the lower, dominates); `rf min_samples_leaf` 18/50 lower; `ftt batch_size` 17/50 lower; `ftt n_blocks` 15/50 lower and 15/50 upper (split evenly).
  4. TabNet's `heart_cleveland` collapses (splits 1 and 7, AUROC 0.736 and 0.673 at fraction 1.0) are **not** fixed by a longer schedule (only split 1 was in the sensitivity check's scope, and it did not resolve as cleanly as `ckd` split 1 did); `ckd` split 1's collapse (0.759) **is** fixed by it (rises to ~0.999, see above).
  5. **Re-checked 2026-11-07 (Phase 3b) against `results/diagnostics/*__mlp__*.json` and `results/phase2c/sensitivity_runs.csv`** (full table: `results/phase3b/epoch_cap_check.csv`). At the **baseline** schedule (600/60/0.15), `mlp` hits its own `max_epochs` cap in 19/50 tasks at fraction 0.1 and 17/50 at fraction 1.0, but the `max_epochs` value at every one of those hits is well below 500 (fraction 0.1: 120, 150 or 200; fraction 1.0: 24, 36, 67, 86 or 120) — i.e. every baseline cap hit is a **budget hit** (the 600-step budget translated via `min(500, ceil(600/steps_per_epoch))` into a per-task cap below 500, confirmed exactly by recomputing the formula per dataset), never the literal 500-epoch hard limit. Under the Phase 2c sensitivity check's longer-budget variants (splits 0-2 only, 15 fits per model/variant/fraction), the 500-epoch hard limit **does** get hit sometimes: `mlp` under `A_long` (2000/150/0.15) hits it in 2/15 fits at fraction 0.1 (out of 4 total cap hits there) and 0/15 at fraction 1.0; `mlp` under `C_long_bigval` hits it in 1/15 at fraction 0.1 and 0/15 at fraction 1.0; `ftt` under `A_long` hits it in 1/15 at fraction 0.1 (out of 1 cap hit) and 0/15 at fraction 1.0; `ftt` under `C_long_bigval` hits it in 1/15 at fraction 0.1. `tabnet` never hits any cap under any variant (0/15 everywhere). So: the baseline results are never affected by the literal 500-epoch limit; only the longer-budget sensitivity variants occasionally are, and only for `mlp`/`ftt` at fraction 0.1.
  6. **Evidence framing for the paper (2026-11-07):** the primary evidence is the paired bootstrap differences to logreg and the Nadeau-Bengio corrected per-dataset t-tests (Phase 3a); the Friedman tests and critical-difference diagrams are **descriptive only**, because the BLOCK unit is anti-conservative (the 10 splits of a dataset come from overlapping-training-set repeated cross-validation) and the DATASET unit has essentially no power (minimum possible two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.0625 with 5 datasets, 0.125 with 4). Every claim in the paper must be scoped to "on these 5 small datasets, with 20 tuning trials per model and a fixed training schedule."
  7. **Phase order (2026-11-07):** 3b (calibration) then 3c (robustness, on the saved models) then 3d (explanations, SHAP), each run in its own cleared Claude Code session per the new section 3 protocol.
  8. **Conference search, 2026-11-07 (information only, target NOT yet chosen):** EMBC 2027 (IEEE EMBS, Singapore, 11-15 July 2027; full contributed paper deadline 24 January 2027, full-paper notification 16 April 2027, camera-ready 30 April 2027; page limit and attendance rules for 2027 must still be checked on the official site — EMBC 2024 allowed up to 7 pages). AiMH 2027 (Maldives, 23-25 March 2027; abstract 30 December 2026, submission 28 February 2027; organised by IFSA; indexing and review standards **not verified**). CHIL 2027 and CBMS 2027 dates **not found** (CHIL 2026 had a 4 February 2026 deadline, so CHIL 2027 is probably early February 2027, **unconfirmed**).
  9. The paper's statements about CKD must say it is saturated, and results must be reported both with and without it (as already done throughout Phase 3a's ALL5/NO_CKD split).
  10. **Phase 3b post-hoc recalibration scope (2026-11-08):** the Phase 3b post-hoc Platt/isotonic results are **exploratory** — cross-fitted on the test predictions themselves (not a pipeline component), with a 12.5% Platt fallback rate (439/3500 fold-fits) and an isotonic clipping artefact (isotonic maps some held-out points to exactly 0/1, inflating log loss when wrong). They get **at most one sentence or a supplementary table** in the paper; no further calibration work is planned.
  11. **Calibration measures for the paper (2026-11-08):** report pooled equal-width ECE (`ece_ew`, the project's own definition) as primary, with pooled equal-mass ECE (`ece_em`) as supplementary, plus log loss, Brier score and the calibration slope. The **per-split mean ECE in the earlier Phase 2a/2b Table 3 is inflated by the small test folds (60-154 rows) and must not be quoted** in the paper — use the Phase 3b pooled values instead.
  12. **Compute-scoping working rule (2026-11-08, from Phase 3b):** scope bootstrap and other heavy computations to the fractions/levels/quantities actually reported before running them, not after — the Phase 3b slope bootstrap ran over all four fractions when only two (1.0, 0.1) were reported, costing about 43.5 minutes for data that was two-thirds unused.
  13. **Phase 3c caveats (2026-11-08):** CKD's noise results are inflated by continuous Gaussian noise applied to the ordinal columns `sg`, `al`, `su` (and Cleveland's `ca`) as if they were continuous; a continuous-only supplementary variant excluding these columns is run in Phase 3d. The largest single-split AUROC drop (`ilpd`, split 1, noise=0.5, draw 2 — the same cell for all 7 models) is a perturbation artefact: Gaussian noise can create physically impossible values (e.g. negative lab values) since no clipping was applied in Phase 3c. The Phase 3c Table 12 summary as printed in that session's final chat message was garbled; the numbers must be taken from `results/phase3c/table12_diff_vs_logreg.csv` only (re-printed cleanly in Phase 3d, see section 6).
  14. **SHAP design, fixed 2026-11-08 BEFORE any SHAP output exists:** families `logreg`, `rf`, `mlp` (the Phase 3a-rule best of each family: linear/trees/deep). Explanations are computed on the ENCODED columns and aggregated back to ORIGINAL features by SUMMING the signed SHAP values of a feature's encoded columns per row, then taking the mean absolute value over test rows. Agreement is measured per dataset and split by top-5 Jaccard and Spearman rank correlation (over all original features) between the 3 model pairs, compared against two baselines: within-model stability across splits, and the chance level (exact expected Jaccard of two random top-5 subsets of M features; expected Spearman 0). Clinical plausibility = precision of the top-5 against the pre-registered list (section 7), compared against chance (list size / M). No direction-of-effect analysis (a stated limitation).

The analysis code verifies the SHA-256 at runtime and refuses to run on a mismatch.
  16. **SHAP-installation fallback rule (2026-11-08):** if the `shap` package cannot be installed into `.venv-deep` without upgrading, downgrading or removing any already-installed package, permutation importance (mean increase in log loss from permuting one original feature, 10 repeats) is used for all three models instead, and the paper must say so.
